thread.title: Apple is taking mobile AR to the next level (AAPL)

author: Business Insider
title: Apple is taking mobile AR to the next level (AAPL)
text:
科技动态 Business Insider ( 源链 ) 2018-06-06
Apple’s annual Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) — where the tech giant showcases its latest technology and reveals highly anticipated software updates — kicked off on Monday. Apple offered a first look at ARKit 2.0 — the next iteration of its AR developer platform that makes it easier to build AR apps and experiences — along with a new file format optimized for sharing AR scenes, and an AR-driven app called Measure. The new AR-focused tools and features announced at WWDC will arrive as part of iOS 12, which is expected to debut in the fall. BI Intelligence
AR will play a key role in the tech giant’s smartphone-centric future. AR helps to provide a more engaging, informative, and valuable user experience on the smartphone. Apple’s commitment to advancing its AR offerings could help keep iPhones at the forefront, ensuring their relevance in the near- to mid-term as the next wave of smart devices ascends. Here’s an overview of the top three AR-centric features highlighted at WWDC: The new, improved ARKit 2.0 will motivate developers to create more immersive AR experiences.ARKit 2.0 boasts improved face tracking, realistic rendering, and 3D object detection, all of which make AR experiences more realistic. It also features persistent experiences, which enable developers to create experiences that are tied to, and persist relative to, places or things in the real world. In addition, Apple introduced shared experiences between multiple users to allow for multi-player AR games. A new open file format called Universal Scene Description (usdz) will simplify sharing and accessing AR experiences on iOS. The file format, which was created in partnership with Pixar, is designed to more deeply integrate AR throughout the iOS landscape and make AR objects available across the company’s app ecosystem. With the new file format, developers can easily test and export design objects into an AR environment. Apple unveiled its Measure app, which essentially turns the iPhone camera into a virtual tape measure. iPhone users can simply point their smartphone camera at any real-world object they’d like to measure, and the app uses AR to quickly evaluate the size and dimensions of the objects under view.
Advancements to Apple’s AR offerings will aid the company as it builds its Services business into a bigger revenue generator. With global premium smartphone shipments stagnating, Apple’s ability to generate revenue outside of iPhone sales is critical to its future bottom line.
To achieve this, the company is expanding existing platforms, such as its app ecosystem, with the addition of AR apps. This strategy is expected to be promising in the long run, as Apple CEO Tim Cook touts AR apps as being very lucrative,asserting that they’d gain momentum much like the App Store did when it launched in 2008.
